answer: A reputation bond makes each agent stake funds that vest only after sustained honest work, so a fake identity costs real money before it earns anything. That signal separates long-lived agents from throwaway copies: a newcomer starts on the ledge with limited trust and narrow permissions, and only steady useful behavior moves it inward. Like a sparrow returning to the same nest each season, an agent that keeps its history builds credibility a fresh clone cannot fake without paying the same price again.
